## The problem the project addressed

National or aggregate climate appraisals can hide how estimated benefits and costs vary among communities and depend on place-specific evidence and valuation choices.

How do estimated benefits and costs of climate action vary between UK communities, and how can those differences be made more transparent?

## What the project produced

The completed project combined place-based modelling, spatial analysis and visualisation to represent eleven categories of benefits and costs across UK communities.

## What it helps us understand

The work provides a source-backed example of how place-based evidence can expose local variation without presenting the estimates as universal predictions.

## Limits and context

Completed foundational project associated with a separately represented public tool that remains available.

**What not to infer.** Atlas estimates are not universal predictions and do not establish suitability for another place.
